newsitem.title: USA: Fissure between big, small U.S. banks widens.
newsitem.headline: Fissure between big, small U.S. banks widens.

text.p: The Independent Bankers Association of America (IBAA) launched a public awareness campaign that emphasizes differences between its small community bank members and mega-state banking organizations, signifying a widening of the fissure between the two groups amid a wave of industry consolidation.

IBAA represents 5,500 independent community banks with 9,823 branches that hold nearly $375 billion in insured deposits, $445 billion in assets, and more than $240 billion in loans for consumers, small businesses and farmers.

"We think there is a need for service down at the local level from bankers that live in the community, understand the community and whose future is tied to that community," Leland Stenehjem, IBAA president said in a telephone interview. "We can serve the smaller business in areas of this country and consumers better than the big boys can."

Asked how the IBAA views the bank consolidation trend in the U.S., which has reduced the number of banking companies to under 10,000 from about 14,000, Stenehjem said "we're generally generally opposed to further consolidation and concentration. We would certainly draw the line at the common ownership of banks and commercial firms." He said the group was analyzing its position on ties between banks on the one hand and securities and insurance firms on the other.
In addition to his role as president of the IBAA, Stenehjem heads First International Bank and Trust Co, a $258 million asset bank company headquartered in Watford City, N.D.

The IBAA has adopted a diamond-shaped logo symbolizing the four points of a compass with roof-like shapes representing four constituencies -- individuals, businesses, farmers and communities. The group will use the slogan "Your Community Bank - On Your Corner, In Your Corner."
